learner_notice: Feedback follows a committed response. The opening activity is informational; an unresolved fresh check returns to planning without credit.

items.title: entry: Explain impression management and dramaturgy
items.prompt: Before meeting donors, a volunteer changes from casual wording to a concise project summary intended to convey preparedness. Which process is most directly illustrated?
options: Impression management for a specific audience
Back-stage release from every audience expectation
Animal signaling through a species-typical display
Sensory adaptation to repeated verbal stimulation
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: guided: Explain impression management and dramaturgy
items.prompt: Which detail is most important when deciding whether a behavior is front-stage performance?
options: The behavior occurs in the front room of a building
A relevant audience can observe the performance
The actor privately rehearsed the behavior on an earlier day
The actor feels completely comfortable during the interaction
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: light: Explain impression management and dramaturgy
items.prompt: A clinical team practices a presentation in an empty conference room before patients arrive. Which classification best fits that practice session?
options: Front-stage performance because a conference room is formal
No social behavior because patients are not yet present
Back-stage preparation for a later audience-facing interaction
Impression management by the patients toward the team
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: solo: Explain impression management and dramaturgy
items.prompt: A speaker sincerely emphasizes different experiences in a job interview than in a reunion conversation. Which interpretation is most defensible?
options: Every change in self-presentation proves the speaker is lying
The two interactions must have identical expectations and goals
Only nonverbal cues can be used for impression management
Audience-specific presentation need not be deceptive
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: near: Explain impression management and dramaturgy
items.prompt: During a grant interview, a researcher displays an organized timeline and uses formal language to appear prepared. What is the clearest interpretation?
options: The researcher is managing an impression before the interview panel
The panel is performing back-stage preparation for the researcher
Formal language proves the research findings are accurate
The timeline removes every social expectation from the interview
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: changed: Explain impression management and dramaturgy
items.prompt: A teaching kitchen is used privately for staff rehearsal in the morning and for a live public demonstration in the afternoon. Which classification is best?
options: Front stage at both times because the room contains demonstration equipment
Back stage during rehearsal and front stage during the public demonstration
Back stage at both times because food preparation occurs there
Neither stage because one physical space cannot change social function
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

Speaker identity, assumed personality, and moral judgment

The checklist proves the coordinator never makes an error

The coordinator presents an organized role to the new-volunteer audience

Treat every workplace room as front stage at all times
Treat every private conversation as dishonest back-stage behavior

options: Both periods are front stage because cameras remain in the studio
Closed rehearsal is back stage; audience broadcast is front stage

items.title: entry: Interpret human communication across gender and culture
items.prompt: A speaker says, 'I agree,' while repeatedly checking the clock. Which observation is nonverbal?
options: The spoken phrase 'I agree'
The grammatical form of the sentence
Repeatedly checking the clock
The dictionary meaning of agreement
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: guided: Interpret human communication across gender and culture
items.prompt: A colleague says a plan is clear, pauses, and asks for the central step again. Which interpretation is best bounded by the evidence?
options: The words prove complete understanding despite the follow-up
The pause proves deliberate deception in every context
The follow-up proves the colleague understood nothing
The channels are mixed, so clarification is warranted
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: light: Interpret human communication across gender and culture
items.prompt: Which feature most directly helps interpret whether a long pause marks reflection or discomfort?
options: The relationship, setting, sequence, and speaker's usual baseline
A universal rule that every long pause has one meaning
The assumption that nonverbal cues are always more truthful
The speaker's identity used without any observed behavior
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: solo: Interpret human communication across gender and culture
items.prompt: A group study reports an average conversational tendency, but one participant's observed baseline differs from that average. Which inference is strongest?
options: Assume the group average determines every individual response
Use observed behavior and context, not a forced group average
Ignore all contextual evidence because group data always has priority
Conclude that all group-level communication research is useless
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: near: Interpret human communication across gender and culture
items.prompt: A manager says, 'Take your time,' but interrupts twice within ten seconds and points toward the door. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: The words alone prove the manager wants an unlimited delay
Pointing always means anger in every culture and setting
The channels conflict, so clarification may be needed
The interruptions prove a stable dishonest personality
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.title: changed: Interpret human communication across gender and culture
items.prompt: A data set shows a group-level difference in average eye contact. One participant consistently uses more eye contact than either group average and does so in the current meeting. What should guide interpretation?
options: The group label alone because averages determine each member
A universal claim that eye contact always communicates confidence
The assumption that any deviation from an average is deceptive
Use the observed baseline and context; keep group data bounded
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

items.prompt: Which order best repairs an overconfident reading of a mixed message?
options: List words, cues, timing, and context before interpreting
Choose one gesture and assign it a universal hidden meaning
Assume the verbal channel is always false when cues conflict
Infer a stable personality from one brief interaction
items.directions: Select one option and commit the choice before feedback is released.

The message is mixed, and one more clarification is reasonable

The request proves complete inability to perform any step

As proof of ability, motive, or personality without local evidence
As context checked against observed behavior and setting
As irrelevant information that can never inform any context

Treat the difference as proof that the participant is deceptive

items.title: entry: Explain animal communication
items.prompt: One animal emits a call and nearby group members move toward cover. Which element is the receiver response?

The first animal produces the call
The call travels through the air
The nearby habitat contains cover

The trail is receiver; route-following is sender; forager is medium
Food is receiver; nestmates are signals; chemistry is response

Tactile signaling

An environmental cue rather than an animal-produced social signal
